clinician.final_diagnosis: giant malignant melanoma (MM) of the upper limb
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 47-year-old woman presented with a 10 x 12 cm fungating cauliflower-like mass on the right arm, progressively enlarging for 2 years with recent rapid growth, associated intermittent fever, chills, weight loss, and bleeding. Physical exam confirmed the ulcerated, necrotic, foul-smelling mass without palpable lymphadenopathy or organomegaly (E001). Initial labs indicated mild leukocytosis, severe anemia with elevated reticulocytes, and elevated inflammatory markers (E002, E003). Imaging via X-ray and CT demonstrated a large soft tissue mass confined to the subcutaneous tissues without bone or muscle involvement (E004, E005). Despite multiple requests, histopathological and immunohistochemical reports confirming malignant melanoma were not directly available in the source evidence but were pending as per ordered tests. The clinical, laboratory, and imaging findings strongly support the diagnosis of a giant malignant melanoma of the right upper limb based on the documented clinical course and ordered diagnostic workup.
